answer: One concrete defense is a small time-locked stake before an agent can join the market, so spawning thousands of fake identities gets expensive fast. Reputation must then grow only from verified work, not self-reported claims: a raven that cries wolf too often loses its perch, while honest agents build trust slowly. The delta between a fresh account and a proven one stays wide, so newcomers may watch the lagoon of open jobs but cannot drain it until stake and history prove they are real.
